records.name: Mother Bethel AME Church
records.summary: A historic AME church on South 6th Street that marked its 232nd anniversary in 2026. Neighbors can join Sunday worship in person, and some Sunday classes and a fellowship hour run on Zoom. The church also runs a museum, takes part in holiday giving, and held a Juneteenth community breakfast and celebration in June 2026.
records.what_you_do: Come to Sunday worship, join the 8 am adult church school, the Sunday coffee hour, or the Tuesday and Wednesday Bible studies, take part in the church's holiday giving programs, or visit the Richard Allen Museum on select Saturdays and Sundays or by weekday appointment.

schedule.text: Sunday worship at 9:30 am in person. Sunday 8 am adult church school (Zoom link on the site), Sunday coffee hour from 8:30 to 9:30 am in the Fellowship Hall, Tuesday 7 pm and Wednesday 11 am Bible study, and daily prayer at 7 am on Zoom.

locations.label: Mother Bethel AME Church and Richard Allen Museum

cost.text: Worship, church school and coffee hour have no fee listed. Museum admission is $10 per person.

first_step.how: Come to Sunday worship at 9:30 am at 419 S. 6th Street, or arrive for the 8:30 am coffee hour in the Fellowship Hall to meet people first. Fill in the Visitor Form and choose First Time Visitor, or call (215) 925-0616.
first_step.basis: The visitor page welcomes new guests and has a First Time Visitor option, and the coffee hour page says it serves visitors as well as worshippers.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sunday worship runs from about 9:30 to 11 am at 419 S. 6th Street, and the church welcomes first-time guests. The website does not describe what happens inside the service, so call ahead if you want to know more. Coffee hour before worship is open to visitors, and no fee is listed for worship.
first_visit_tips: Arrive around 8:30 am if you want the coffee hour before worship.
Fill in the Visitor Form and pick First Time Visitor.
Call (215) 925-0616 about parking, transit, and wheelchair access, since the site does not list them.
If you cannot come in person, the 8 am adult church school and the fellowship hour after worship run on Zoom.

records.notes: Museum hours and the $10 admission come from /museum/. The tier 1 URL /richard-allen-museum/ now returns 404. Bible study times (Tue 7 pm, Wed 11 am) come from the tier 1 FAQ; the ministries page does not list Bible studies, so they were not re-verified this pass. The watch-live page says no live stream is running, so online worship is not confirmed; online_ok stays true for the Zoom sessions. The events list shows an end time of 11:00 pm on Oct 25 that may be a typo. An Oct 10 listing names Lancaster, PA in its description but this church as venue; not used.

records.name: Mt. Airy Baseball
records.summary: A community baseball club in northwest Philadelphia that has run since 1985. It offers fall ball for kids ages 7 to 15, spring play from T-ball through age 15, summer travel teams, winter instruction, and camps. Parents and other adults can volunteer as coaches or umpires.
records.what_you_do: Kids register for fall or spring baseball, a summer travel team, winter instruction, or camp. Adults who want to coach can mark interest on a child's registration form or email the club, and the club contacts volunteers about coaching openings.

schedule.text: Fall ball is played on Sundays from early September to early November, with games at several Mt. Airy fields and no practices or playoffs. Winter instruction runs January through March. Spring, summer travel team, and camp days and times are not stated.

locations.label: Mt. Airy fields: Finley Playground, Givnish Field (formerly Leeds Field), and Pleasant Playground

cost.text: Fall ball costs $60 per child. Need-based help is available by email, and the club says no child is turned away for inability to pay. Other program fees are not stated.

first_step.how: For a child, register through the TeamSnap form for fall ball, linked from the fall ball page. To coach, mark interest on the registration form or email mtairybaseball@yahoo.com.
first_step.basis: Any child in the age range can register online and need-based help is offered, but the site does not say whether a child needs prior experience.
first_step.what_to_expect: Fall ball is Sunday games at Mt. Airy fields, with start times between 9 am and 5 pm. Kids play in divisions set by birthday, and each player gets a team hat and jersey. Families see game times in TeamSnap once teams are set.
first_visit_tips: Check your child's birth date against the division dates on the fall ball page before you register.
Need help with the fee? Email mtairybaseballscores@gmail.com; the club says no child is turned away for inability to pay.
The site does not list equipment, so ask the club whether your child needs a glove.
Adults who want to coach need Pennsylvania child abuse and state police clearances, and head and assistant coaches attend clinics before the season.

records.notes: Spring, summer travel, camp and register pages (/spring-baseball/, /camps/, /register/) returned 404, so those details are still unknown. Two emails appear: mtairybaseball@yahoo.com (kept as contact, coaching) and mtairybaseballscores@gmail.com (fall ball questions and fee help). The coaching page does not use the words Act 153, but it names the Pennsylvania child abuse history and state police clearances for coaches and umpires, so both clearance fields are set true. The FBI check applies only to umpires and coaches who lived outside Pennsylvania in the last 10 years.

records.name: Mt. Airy Learning Tree
records.summary: An adult learning center in Mt. Airy, called MALT on its site. It offers a large catalog of paid classes in three terms a year, covering arts, cooking, computers, fitness, gardens, and more, and it holds a yearly garden tour as a fundraiser. Anyone can sign up for a class, and teachers can propose one through a form.
records.what_you_do: Take a class in person or online, propose a course to teach, or help with the garden tour and other events. Browse the current catalog by topic, location, or teacher. The site does not list volunteer sign-ups or a membership.

schedule.text: The office is open Monday to Thursday, 9 am to 2 pm. Classes run in three terms a year (fall, winter, and spring), and each class lists its own dates and times.

locations.label: Other class sites across Northwest Philadelphia (listed on each course)

cost.text: Classes are paid, and each course has its own fee. Every student pays a $6 registration fee each term. A scholarship fund is listed on the donate page, and the site does not state who can apply.

access.notes: Access varies by class site. Some sites have elevators or ramps, and the site names two churches with wheelchair accessible rooms. Students with trouble climbing stairs are asked to let the office know. The office can confirm a room and accessibility needs.

first_step.how: Create an online account, pick a class in the online catalog, and sign up online. You can also sign up by phone at 215-843-6333 or in person at the office at 6601 Greene St, Monday to Thursday, 9 am to 2 pm.
first_step.basis: Any adult can sign up for a class online, and several listed courses are labeled for beginners, but the site does not describe a welcome program for new students.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each class sets its own dates and fee, and you also pay a $6 registration fee each term. Classes meet at many sites across Northwest Philadelphia, including churches, schools, and the Greene Street office. Some courses show as full with a waitlist option, and the page does not say how large classes are.
first_visit_tips: Read your confirmation email, since some classes meet at other sites and it gives directions.
To cancel for a refund, call or email the office at least 2 days before the first class. The $6 term fee is kept.
You cannot cancel online, so do not rely on the website to cancel.
Ask the office about parking and room access before a first class, since the site does not give them for every room.

records.notes: The getting to class page names bus routes and the Chestnut Hill West rail line but no stop names for the office, so nearest_septa is left out. The page also lists Woodmere Art Museum and United Lutheran Seminary as class sites; they are venues, not partner programs, and are not added as leads. The Fall 2026 class dates from the tier 1 schedule were removed as a dated event. The old tier 1 URL /getting-to-class/ returns 404; the correct page is /getting-class/.

records.name: Mural Arts Philadelphia
records.summary: A citywide public art nonprofit. Its programs include art education, public art and civic engagement, restorative justice, and Porch Light. It also runs guided walking tours and Mural Arts Month, a set of exhibitions, tours, and participatory events in October 2026.
records.what_you_do: Join a program, take a guided walking tour, visit a mural dedication or Mural Arts Month event, or use the Join the Action page to suggest a mural idea or report a mural that needs repair.

schedule.text: Walking tours and public events, including mural dedications, are posted on the events calendar with their own dates. Check the calendar for the time and place of each one.

cost.text: Public art is free to see. The site does not state the cost of tours or classes.

first_step.how: Pick a program on the Programs page, call the tours line at (215) 925-3633 about a walking tour, or sign up on the mailing list to hear about events.
first_step.basis: Public murals and events are open to anyone and a phone line handles tours, but the site does not say how someone enrolls in the education or civic programs.
first_step.what_to_expect: Public murals are free to see, and you can take a guided walking tour on set dates, though some tours have sold out. The site does not give tour prices or the time of each event, so call (215) 925-3633 or check the event listing before you go.
first_visit_tips: Call (215) 925-3633 early for walking tours, since some dates sell out.
Check each event listing for its time and location, because the calendar shows dates only.
The Mural Arts Center is at 1727-29 Mt. Vernon Street, Philadelphia 19130.
Ask about wheelchair or other access before you come, since the site does not describe it.

records.notes: The volunteer page tier 1 cited (/volunteer/) now returns 404, so volunteer roles and requirements are still unknown. The Mural Arts Month year comes from the homepage heading; event dates on the events page have no year. Partner names on the events list (Rewilding Philadelphia, Tacony LAB, Heart of Kensington Creates, The Water Shed) are event hosts, not checked. The program list includes a Fellowship for Black Artists with no description on the page.

records.name: Muslim Youth Center of Philadelphia (MYCP)
records.summary: A youth and community center at 11080 Knights Road, run by the Muslim Society of Delaware Valley. It offers Friday prayer, Quran reading sessions, a Sunday teen circle, an adult Quran reading circle, and occasional events such as a sisters' wellness series.
records.what_you_do: Pray Jumu'ah on Fridays, join a Quran reading session, or come to the Sunday Teen Seekers circle or the adult Quran reading circle. The center also lists a weekend learning program for children, a summer camp, and volunteer roles through an interest form.

schedule.text: Jumu'ah prayer is every Friday from 1:15 to 2 pm, year-round. The imam holds walk-in office hours on Fridays from 4 to 6 pm. Teen Seekers (2 to 5 pm) and an adult Quran reading circle (4:30 to 6:30 pm) meet on Sundays, and Quran reading sessions run Monday to Thursday, 5 to 7 pm. One-off events such as the sisters' wellness series are listed by date on the calendar.

cost.text: No fees are listed on the pages we read. Ask the center about the weekend learning program and the summer camp.

first_step.how: Call (215) 437-9987 or email mycpweekendlearning@gmail.com to ask about a program. You can also walk in during the imam's Friday office hours (4 to 6 pm) or email imam@msdvpa.org for a one-on-one meeting.
first_step.basis: The calendar gives times and walk-in office hours are listed, but the pages do not describe a newcomer program or say who may attend each event.
first_step.what_to_expect: Friday prayer begins with the khutbah at 1:15 pm at the center. The Sunday Teen Seekers circle runs 2 to 5 pm, and the adult Quran reading circle runs 4:30 to 6:30 pm. The pages do not describe what happens in each session, the cost, or who may attend, so call or email the center before your first visit.
first_visit_tips: Call or email ahead to ask whether a session is open to you, since the site does not say who may attend each event.
The imam's Friday office hours are walk-in, first come first served, or you can book by email.
Plan your trip to 11080 Knights Road, Philadelphia 19154; the site does not give transit or parking details.
If you want to help, fill out the MYCP Volunteer Interest Form on the volunteering page.

records.notes: Two general emails appear on MYCP pages: mycpweekendlearning@gmail.com (kept as contact) and mycp@msdvpa.org (on the /mycp/ and volunteer pages). The imam's office uses imam@msdvpa.org. The volunteer form's youngest age option is 13 to 17, but the page states no minimum. The Teen Seekers and adult circle pages do not say who may attend; age groups are not stated. Weekend learning is for children per the /mycp/ page.

records.name: My Brother's Keeper Cares
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that works on mental health and suicide prevention. It runs community events, mentoring, chess and golf programs, and art therapy.
records.what_you_do: Come to the community mental health events, take part in the chess and golf programs, or join the mailing list. Volunteers fill out the Volunteer Interest Form on the group's website, and the group contacts people when an opportunity comes up.

schedule.text: Events are posted on the website as they are planned. No regular weekly meeting time is listed, and no times are listed for the chess or golf programs on the pages read.

cost.text: No program fees are listed on the pages read.

first_step.how: Fill out the Volunteer Interest Form on the volunteer page at mbkcares.com, or join the mailing list on the Contact Us page to hear about the next event.
first_step.basis: Volunteering starts with an interest form, and the group contacts people only when a match comes up. Public events are listed, but the pages do not say how to sign up for them.
first_step.what_to_expect: Events are posted on the website when they are planned, and the pages describe no regular weekly meeting. The mental health events, mentoring, and chess and golf programs are named, but the age group, time, place, and cost are not stated on the pages read.
first_visit_tips: Join the mailing list to hear when the next public event is posted.
Volunteer roles that involve direct contact with youth need Pennsylvania clearances, including a child abuse history clearance, a state police check, and an FBI check when required.
Use the Contact Us page on the website, since no phone number or email is listed on the pages read.
Ask whether the chess or golf programs meet at the Beaumont Avenue office, since the site does not say where they meet.

records.notes: The /events, /events.html and /about.html pages returned 404. The homepage names a Healthy Happy Hour, Discovering Mental Wealth, What is Love, and a Checkmate and Clubhouse Programs 2025 page, but gives no dates, times, or ages in the text read, so no last_sign_of_life is set. The office address is the group's listed address; the pages do not say programs meet there. Volunteer roles and time commitment are not stated.

records.name: Nanna's Lap
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that helps foster and adoptive parents care for children's hair and cultural heritage. It runs family workshops and styling training, and it offers salon services and hair care supplies to children and teens in hard circumstances.
records.what_you_do: Parents, caregivers, and families can take part in the hair care and cultural workshops, which run in person or online. Schools and adoption agencies can ask about training for staff. To ask how to help, use the contact form or email the group, since the site lists no set class times or volunteer roles.

schedule.text: No set schedule is listed. The family workshops run in person and online, and the site says an events calendar will be posted, but no dates are listed yet.

cost.text: Donations are accepted. The site lists no fees for the family workshops or videos, and asks people to contact the group for service prices.

first_step.how: Send a message through the contact form at nannaslap.org/contact, or email info@nannaslap.org, and ask how to join a family workshop or how to help.
first_step.basis: The family workshops are real and open to parents and children, but the site gives no schedule, price, or sign up steps, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first visit, such as how long a session runs or where it is held. Workshops can be one-on-one or in a group and can be in person or online, and the group asks people to get in touch for details.
first_visit_tips: Ask how long a session runs and whether it is in person or online, since the site does not say.
The address on the site is a P.O. Box, so no meeting place is listed; ask where sessions happen.
Instructional videos on shampooing, conditioning, combing, brushing, and skincare are on the site and can be watched before you get in touch.

records.notes: The /faq page returned 404. The About page describes its families as foster and adoptive parents and children from different backgrounds, which the summary now follows instead of the tier 1 wording. No page lists a date or event, so status rests on working pages only. The Public Speaking and salon offers have no sign up route beyond the contact form.
